content.jointProblem: Where should Serbian Cyrillic–Latin normalisation be applied in KlozuraPro’s PostgreSQL search pipeline—at indexing, query time, or both—to reduce script-related missed results without unacceptable false matches or latency? The first experiment would test transfer of the researcher’s tabular-record normaliser to labelled contract-search cases, including mixed-script text and ambiguous Latin sequences, and compare these pipeline variants against current search.

rationale.text: Ranković has directly relevant experience developing Serbian Cyrillic–Latin normalisation and diacritic-tolerant comparison for entity resolution, providing a concrete starting point rather than a validated contract-search solution.

sources.quote: incorporating a rule-based Cyrillic–Latin normaliser, a diacritic-robust string distance metric derived from Jaro–Winkler

rationale.text: Her group works with PostgreSQL and Python-based matching frameworks, aligning with the company’s database and NLP implementation environment.

sources.quote: The group works with PostgreSQL, Python-based matching frameworks, and RDF triple stores

rationale.text: Her benchmark-construction experience supports designing an annotated evaluation set that distinguishes script-related retrieval failures from other search errors.

sources.quote: A benchmark comprising 22 schema pairs derived from Serbian and Croatian administrative sources was assembled and manually annotated by three independent experts

constraints.text: The implementation must integrate with the existing PostgreSQL full-text search and Python NLP pipeline; the project must explicitly compare indexing-time and query-time placement.

sources.quote: PostgreSQL with full-text search for document storage
Python-based NLP pipeline (spaCy, custom fine-tuned transformer models trained on Serbian-language contracts)
at indexing time, at query time, or both

constraints.text: Correctness testing must cover mixed-script documents and ambiguous Latin-to-Cyrillic mappings, not only whole-document transliteration.

sources.quote: robust enough to handle mixed-script documents, not just fully-Cyrillic or fully-Latin ones
the same Latin sequence maps to different Cyrillic letters depending on dialect conventions

constraints.text: Search latency is a deployment acceptance requirement; the company must define a measurable threshold for what counts as a noticeable slowdown.

sources.quote: does not slow down search response times noticeably

constraints.text: Scope must fit a backend engineer’s six-week contribution and the company’s capacity for only one external project alongside product development.

sources.quote: We have one backend engineer who can work on this for up to six weeks.
capacity for roughly one external project at a time alongside normal product development

constraints.text: The researcher’s moderate capacity favours a tightly scoped short-term engagement with a concrete dataset rather than a large coordination role.

sources.quote: Currently co-supervising two PhD students, so capacity for new commitments is moderate
shorter-term contract research or clearly scoped consulting arrangements are more feasible than new large project coordination roles in the near term.
Prefers projects where there is a concrete dataset to work with rather than purely theoretical engagements.

risks: The published normaliser was evaluated on voter-registration record pairs, not contract full-text retrieval. Mixed-script tokenisation, legal terminology and PostgreSQL ranking may behave differently; the first experiment must establish whether transfer is useful.
Normalisation may introduce false matches or alter ranking when ambiguous sequences or diacritic distinctions are collapsed; fewer zero-hit searches alone would not establish better retrieval.
The reported one-in-five failure estimate comes from a January 2024 log sample and may not represent current traffic or isolate script mismatch from other causes.
Researcher availability for the proposed six-week window is unknown despite openness to joint projects and the stated moderate capacity.
Access to representative contracts, queries and relevance labels, permission to use them, and project budget are unknown; delays could consume the limited engineering window.
questions: Can Ranković commit to a scoped joint project during the company’s six-week engineering window, and how much supervision or implementation time can she provide?
Can the company provide representative parsed contracts and query logs, including mixed-script and ambiguous cases, with relevance judgements and appropriate confidentiality and access arrangements?
What are the current PostgreSQL version, text-search configuration, tokenisation rules, index size, query volume and latency distribution?
What thresholds should govern retrieval quality, false matches, ranking changes and p95 search latency, and who will validate ambiguous legal-search cases?
Can the existing normalisation implementation be reused, and under what licence or intellectual-property terms?
What budget, ML-engineer support, reindexing window and deployment or rollback arrangements are available?
